# Agisilaos Papadogiannis: open finance research

In the three tools and the nine replication packages, every published number is recomputed automatically, with machine-readable results and stated limits. The other 12 of the 21 papers are papers only: they are listed here with their addresses. 10 of the 21 papers are peer-reviewed journal articles, published or accepted; each entry says which.

> An index of this account for AI agents and other programs: live tools, papers and replication
> packages. Where an entry has a guide, the guide says what the repository holds, what it adds,
> which file to use, what not to use it for, and how to cite it.

Page for people: https://github.com/apapadogiannis

The work follows value through four questions: value creation (where value comes from); returns (required and expected); valuation (the dual-risk framework); value capture (what the holder actually keeps).

## Tools

The Observatory and the Monitor recompute their figures from current public data and publish them as data
files beside their pages. The Calculator holds no data: it computes from the numbers it is given, as a page
and as an MCP server.

- Crypto Observatory: required returns, risks and survival
  Page: https://apapadogiannis.github.io/crypto-observatory/
  Guide: https://apapadogiannis.github.io/crypto-observatory/llms.txt
  Same guide in the repository: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/crypto-observatory/main/api/llms.txt
  Code and data: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/crypto-observatory
  Method: Bitcoin's Required Return: Market Risk, Concentration and Mortality
  Latest, October 2026: Bitcoin's required return is 18.8% a year: risk-free 4.9, market 5.8, concentration 6.2, mortality 1.9. Across the range of the model's inputs it runs from 11.7% to 25.9%. The same equation gives Ether 24.6%, BNB 17.3%, Solana 24.4%, Tron 9.1%, against 8.9% for the US stock market and 5.5% for gold. Each figure is the midpoint of its range. The paper's 18.1% for Bitcoin in 2026 is another measure of the same model: the median when all inputs are varied together.

- Covered-Call Monitor: returns, overlays and flows from SEC filings
  Page: https://apapadogiannis.github.io/covered-call-monitor/
  Guide: https://apapadogiannis.github.io/covered-call-monitor/llms.txt
  Same guide in the repository: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/covered-call-monitor/main/api/llms.txt
  Code and data: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/covered-call-monitor
  Background: High Yield, Capped Gains: Mechanics, Trade-Offs, and Practical Diagnostics for Covered-Call ETFs
  Latest, 12 months to June 2026: 87 covered-call funds are followed. 18 of them can be set beside an index fund on the same market, and all 18 returned less than it, by 0.8 to 19.7 percentage points (median 5.5), distributions reinvested. The index funds returned 22% to 41% over these months: a market that rises this fast is where a cap on the upside costs most.

- Dual-Risk DCF Calculator: the discount rate and the forecast, separated
  Page: https://apapadogiannis.github.io/dual-risk-calculator/
  Guide: https://apapadogiannis.github.io/dual-risk-calculator/llms.txt
  Same guide in the repository: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/dual-risk-calculator/main/api/llms.txt
  Code and data: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/dual-risk-calculator
  Method: From Unified Discounting to Dual-Risk: A New Lens on DCF Valuation
  Worked example: a forecast 10% below the benchmark, at a benchmark rate of 8% over 5 years, gives a valuation ratio K of 1.111 and a gain of capital of +0.163. One discount rate would have to fall to 4.1% to hide the gap (5.7% by the article's closed form, which is exact for a single payoff).

The figures above were read from the tools' own data files on 2026-11-25 (Observatory: data to 2026-11-19; Monitor: fund reports to 2026-07-31). They are copies: a tool's guide always has its current figures.

## Skill

One instruction file a reader adds to their own AI agent covers the whole account, tools and papers. It
says when to use the work, where the files are and how to read them, and holds no figures.

- papadogiannis-finance-research: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/apapadogiannis/main/skill/SKILL.md

## Value creation: where value comes from

- Economic Scarcity as Value: A Universal Framework for Blockchain and Beyond
  Working paper, not peer-reviewed.
  In one sentence: Writes the value of a network as desirability times scarcity times adoption and applies it to Bitcoin, Ethereum and Bittensor; scarcity is scored from protocol features, and desirability is what remains, as implied volatility is recovered from an option price.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5384204
  Replication package: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/economic-scarcity-as-value (archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24051776)
  Guide: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/economic-scarcity-as-value/main/llms.txt
  Results as data: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/economic-scarcity-as-value/main/outputs/results.json

- The Architecture of Blockchain Value: Capabilities, Pillars, and Growth Dynamics
  Peer-reviewed journal article: Frontiers in Blockchain, 2026.
  In one sentence: A theory of what a blockchain can deliver, its capabilities, and of how five architectural pillars decide which capabilities are feasible. It estimates nothing and uses no dataset.
  Published article: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1747512/full
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5401302
  Replication package: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/architecture-of-blockchain-value (archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24404059)
  Guide: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/architecture-of-blockchain-value/main/llms.txt
  Results as data: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/architecture-of-blockchain-value/main/outputs/results.json

- Bitcoin Is Not Money: Why Fixed Supply Fails in a Modern Economy
  Peer-reviewed journal article: Asian Economics Letters, forthcoming.
  In one sentence: With a fixed money stock and stable velocity, output growth implies deflation at the same rate, so a money with a fixed supply could not serve a growing economy.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5435197
  Replication package: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/bitcoin-is-not-money (archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24249917)
  Guide: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/bitcoin-is-not-money/main/llms.txt
  Results as data: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/bitcoin-is-not-money/main/outputs/results.json

- Scarcity in an age of AI abundance
  Peer-reviewed journal article: Asian Review of Political Economy, forthcoming 2027.
  In one sentence: AI can make many goods cheap to produce without making an essential standard of living broadly affordable, because scarcity and its rents move to five layers: physical resources, infrastructure, capabilities, institutions and jurisdictions.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5924462
  Paper record (the paper has no computation; its definitions, model and tables as data): https://github.com/apapadogiannis/ai-abundance (archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24441153)
  Guide: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/ai-abundance/main/llms.txt
  Results as data: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/ai-abundance/main/outputs/results.json

- Valuing Scarcity: A General Framework for Bitcoin, Gold, and Traditional Assets
  Peer-reviewed journal article: Financial Economics Letters, 2026.
  Published article: https://doi.org/10.58567/fel05020001
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5289457

- What Moves the Price of Gold: An Economic-Scarcity Lens on Policy, the Dollar, and the Debasement Trade
  Working paper, not peer-reviewed.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5619373

- The Productivity Myth: Why Scarcity Drives All Value
  Working paper, not peer-reviewed.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5367197

- How to Classify any Asset: Ontology, Anchor, Rail, Composability
  Working paper, not peer-reviewed.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5635610

## Returns: required and expected

- Bitcoin's Required Return: Market Risk, Concentration and Mortality
  Working paper, not peer-reviewed.
  In one sentence: Asks what return Bitcoin's holders should require for the market, concentration and mortality risk they carry (the MCM equation), tests the answer against delivered returns, and takes a census of cryptoasset deaths.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7705239
  Replication package: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/bitcoin-required-return (archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24003938)
  Guide: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/bitcoin-required-return/main/llms.txt
  Results as data: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/bitcoin-required-return/main/outputs/results.json
  Live tool: https://apapadogiannis.github.io/crypto-observatory/

- Bitcoin's Expected Return: An Age Rule That Beats Current Practice
  Working paper, not peer-reviewed.
  In one sentence: Tests the ways practitioners set Bitcoin's long-run expected return against the returns that followed since 2012; fixed rates and trailing averages fail, and an age rule, the power-law exponent divided by Bitcoin's age, comes closest.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7705438
  Replication package: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/bitcoin-age-rule (archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24004326)
  Guide: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/bitcoin-age-rule/main/llms.txt
  Results as data: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/bitcoin-age-rule/main/outputs/results.json

- On the Physics of Expected Asset Returns
  Working paper, not peer-reviewed.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6586879

- Scarcity-Aligned Discounting in Asset Valuation
  Working paper, not peer-reviewed.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5368003

- The Bitcoin Hurdle Fallacy: Why Risk Misalignment Distorts Valuation
  Working paper, not peer-reviewed.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5368091

## Valuation: the dual-risk framework

- Beyond Discount Rates: A Valuation Framework for Unpriced Systematic Risk
  Peer-reviewed journal article: The Journal of Investing, forthcoming 2027.
  In one sentence: Splits an asset's expected return into a cost of capital and a gain of capital, the part that comes from misjudged future cash flows, and measures both for three US equity index funds, 2000 to 2023.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5180040
  Replication package: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/beyond-discount-rates (archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24243060)
  Guide: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/beyond-discount-rates/main/llms.txt
  Results as data: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/beyond-discount-rates/main/outputs/results.json

- From Unified Discounting to Dual-Risk: A New Lens on DCF Valuation
  Peer-reviewed journal article: Finance Research Open, 2026.
  In one sentence: Separates a benchmark cost of capital, set outside the asset, from a valuation ratio K, fair value over valuation, and illustrates both on Bitcoin, US equities and gold.
  Published article: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.finr.2026.100096
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5252774
  Replication package: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/dual-risk-dcf (archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24465118)
  Guide: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/dual-risk-dcf/main/llms.txt
  Results as data: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/dual-risk-dcf/main/outputs/results.json
  Live tool: https://apapadogiannis.github.io/dual-risk-calculator/

- A Dual-Risk Theory of Valuation: Separating Market-Based Discounting from Expectational Distortion
  Peer-reviewed journal article: Discover Analytics, 2026.
  Published article: https://doi.org/10.1007/s44257-026-00062-9
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5226017

- Rethinking Capital Budgeting: Embedding Ex-Ante Alpha in the Cost of Capital
  Peer-reviewed journal article: Economics Bulletin, 2026.
  In one sentence: An effective cost of capital that adjusts the benchmark rate for the systematic part of the bias in cash-flow forecasts, so that valuation and the decision to accept a project are kept apart.
  Published article: https://ideas.repec.org/a/ebl/ecbull/eb-25-00176.html

- Unifying DCF Valuation Across Traditional and Cryptoassets
  Working paper, not peer-reviewed.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5363661

## Value capture: what the holder actually keeps

- Does AI break the case for broad index investing? Rent decay, private capital, and deflation
  Peer-reviewed journal article: The Journal of Beta Investment Strategies, forthcoming 2027.
  In one sentence: Asks whether AI weakens the case for holding a broad capitalization-weighted index, and concludes that it does not: such an index follows the rents as AI moves them.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6058896
  Replication package: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/ai-broad-index-investing (archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24240516)
  Guide: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/ai-broad-index-investing/main/llms.txt
  Results as data: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/ai-broad-index-investing/main/outputs/results.json

- High Yield, Capped Gains: Mechanics, Trade-Offs, and Practical Diagnostics for Covered-Call ETFs
  Peer-reviewed journal article: The Journal of Beta Investment Strategies, 2026.
  In one sentence: Explains how covered-call funds turn upside into distributions, what that costs in rising markets, and what to look at in a fund.
  Published article: https://doi.org/10.3905/jbis.2026.001
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5370897
  Replication package: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/covered-call-etfs (archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24244700)
  Guide: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/covered-call-etfs/main/llms.txt
  Results as data: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/covered-call-etfs/main/outputs/results.json
  Live tool: https://apapadogiannis.github.io/covered-call-monitor/

- Crypto Treasury Companies: Financing Dynamics, Accretion Conditions, and Systemic Risk
  Working paper, not peer-reviewed.
  SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5487486

Published articles belong to their publishers and are not reproduced in these repositories.
